subject: Architecture
title: The Woolworth Building: Cathedral of Commerce
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Woolworth Building: Cathedral of Commerce.

hook.text: Frank Woolworth paid $13.5 million in cash for the world's tallest building — no mortgage.

buildup.text: At 792 feet, the Woolworth Building was the tallest in the world from 1913 to 1930.

discovery.text: Architect Cass Gilbert clad a steel frame in Gothic terracotta — a skyscraper dressed as a cathedral.

twist.text: Inside the lobby, a sculpture shows Woolworth counting nickels — he built his empire on five-cent stores.

climax.text: A minister called it the 'Cathedral of Commerce,' and the nickname stuck permanently.

punchline.text: He sold everything for five cents. Then built the tallest thing on Earth.

quiz.question: How did Woolworth pay for the world's tallest building?
options: A consortium of banks provided the financing
He paid $13.5 million in cash with no mortgage
He traded stock in his retail company

details.summary: The Woolworth Building, completed in 1913 in New York, was the world's tallest at 241 meters and was nicknamed the Cathedral of Commerce for its Gothic-inspired terra cotta exterior. Frank Woolworth paid the entire $13.5 million cost in cash, with no mortgage.
details.whyItMatters: The Woolworth Building proved that a skyscraper could be both a functional office building and a work of art. Its Gothic styling elevated commercial architecture to the status of civic monument.
takeaways: Completed in 1913 as the world's tallest at 241 meters
Gothic terra cotta exterior earned it 'Cathedral of Commerce'
Frank Woolworth paid the full cost in cash

faq.question: Why did the Woolworth Building use Gothic styling?
faq.answer: Architect Cass Gilbert believed Gothic verticality was the natural expression of a tall building. The pointed arches, tracery, and soaring lines of Gothic cathedrals translated naturally to a skyscraper's upward thrust, creating a coherent visual logic for height.

faq.question: How long was the Woolworth Building the world's tallest?
faq.answer: It held the record for 17 years, from 1913 until the Chrysler Building surpassed it in 1930. Its extended reign cemented it as a New York landmark and established the skyscraper height race as a defining feature of American urbanism.
